context_requirements: Cells must express adenylyl cyclase isoforms (ADCY1-9) and have basal or stimulated cAMP signaling for inhibition to have an effect.
Adenylyl cyclase inhibitors such as SQ22536 are relatively weak and may require high intracellular concentrations; 10 µM may be insufficient in many lines.
Cell lines with low basal cAMP or that rely primarily on other proliferative pathways may show minimal transcriptional response.
The response may be more apparent in cells with active Gs-coupled receptor signaling or in the presence of a cAMP-elevating agent.
falsifiers: No significant change in any of the proximal_up or proximal_down genes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines.
A strong and consistent upregulation of cAMP-responsive genes (e.g., CREB1, FOS, JUN, PCK2) across multiple lines, which would suggest cAMP elevation rather than inhibition.
A clear increase in proliferation markers (e.g., CCND1, MYC, PCNA) at 24 h, opposite to the expected anti-proliferative effect.
Lack of any transcriptional response in A549 and MCF7, which are expected to be among the more responsive lines.

evidence.supports: The adenylyl cyclase inhibitor SQ22536 counteracted forskolin-mediated anticancer effects in A549 NSCLC cells, demonstrating that adenylyl cyclase inhibition can modulate proliferation and migration in a relevant cell line.
An adenylyl cyclase inhibitor was used pharmacologically to probe cAMP signaling in immune cells, supporting the use of such inhibitors to modulate cellular responses.
An adenylyl cyclase inhibitor (2',4'-dideoxyadenosine) was used to block cAMP production in retinal neuroprotection studies, confirming its utility as a tool compound.
